To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
color superconductivity in quark matter leads to a stiffening of the equation of state and that this effect is enhanced by a strong flavor mixing interaction.

(i) color superconducting quark phases in compact stars are energetically favorable, (ii) the strange quark matter hypothesis is not supported by NJL-type models, unless a strong flavor mixing is present in the quark sector, (iii) the maximum mass of compact stars is not a direct probe for the equation of state of quark matter, (iv) the maximum mass and radii of compact stars can be used to put constraints on the equation of state, and

the interior of compact stars can be described by a quantum field theory of quarks and gluons and that color superconductivity plays a crucial role for the equation of state and for the thermodynamic properties of the matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (a) How do quark flavor and color degrees of freedom change the equation of state of quark matter?

the following questions: What is the equation of state for dense quark matter and how do the quarks interact? What is the role of color superconductivity in quark matter? What is the structure of hybrid stars? How do the quark interactions and color superconductivity affect the structure of hybrid star interiors? What are the observational consequences for the mass–radius relationship of hybrid stars?
the question of whether or not the interior of compact stars may contain quark matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present data do not allow for a definite conclusion whether or not the strange quark matter hypothesis is correct.
the present status of the physics of compact star interiors is still in its infancy.

hybrid star models are possible and that the quark matter phase in the interior of compact stars can be color superconducting, but that the precise nature of the quark matter and the properties of the hybrid star model are still open issues, which require further investigations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interior of compact stars is not a simple matter, but a very complex one.

the NJL-type model with a Kobayashi–Masakawa–'t Hooft determinant interaction provides a good description for the equation of state of quark matter, including color superconductivity, and can be applied for hybrid star models.
color superconductivity has to be taken into account in order to obtain a realistic equation of state for hybrid star matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

compact stars are not just interesting astrophysical objects, but can also be used as a laboratory to explore fundamental physics at densities far beyond those accessible at present in particle accelerators.
compact star interiors are very rich in their structure, and the physics of dense quark matter is far from being understood.
color superconductivity is a key ingredient in compact star models, and that the strange quark phase is likely not realized in compact star interiors.
